questions.q: Hex-1-ene is treated with (i) 9-BBN in THF and (ii) H₂O₂/NaOH. The main product is:
questions.explain: The bulky borane places boron almost only on the terminal carbon, and oxidation replaces B by OH, giving the anti-Markovnikov alcohol. 9-BBN suppresses the small amount of hexan-2-ol seen with plain BH₃.

questions.q: Each 9-BBN molecule hydroborates only one alkene molecule, whereas BH₃ can add to three. The reason is that 9-BBN:
options: is a Lewis base rather than a Lewis acid
has only one B–H bond, being a dialkylborane R₂BH
questions.explain: In 9-BBN two of boron's bonds are tied up in the bicyclic ring, leaving a single B–H bond, so it cannot form trialkylboranes as BH₃ does.

questions.q: 9-BBN is prepared by double hydroboration of which compound with borane in THF?
questions.explain: Both C=C bonds of cycloocta-1,5-diene add to the same boron; the second addition is intramolecular and locks the ring into the bicyclo[3.3.1] skeleton.

questions.q: Which statement about hydroboration–oxidation with 9-BBN is INCORRECT?
options: Boron adds to the less substituted alkene carbon
A carbocation intermediate forms, so rearranged alcohols are common
H and B add to the same face of the C=C (syn addition)
The alkyl group migrates from B to O with retention of configuration
questions.explain: The B–H adds in one concerted four-centred step; no carbocation forms, so there is no rearrangement. The other three statements are correct.
